rv.q: Her latest, “Benevolent,” at the IATI Theater in the East Village, is set at a fictional Manhattan women’s reformatory in 1917, evoking the feminist reclamation of trapped-women tropes popularized by works like “Girl, Interrupted.”
After seeing her latest, benevolent, I will vehemently state that this and any future play by Sophie McIntosh constitutes must-see theatre.
With Nina Goodheart’s richly calibrated direction, benevolent becomes a remarkably nimble comedy-drama about women discovering one another beneath the categories that society has imposed upon them.
I hope this vital new historical play returns for a longer run.
Goodheart’s deftness with tonal complexity is a key component of the play’s effectiveness.
Goodheart’s sensitive production confirms this company’s precision in bringing tonally tricky, women-led stories to the stage.

August 20, 2026. Jed Ryan benevolent Makes World Premiere at NYC: A Review benevolent , the bold new drama by Sophie McIntosh , is making its World Premiere at IATI Theater in New York City, presented by Good Apples Collective and directed by Nina Goodheart.
Worse yet, we leave the theater feeling like we've just spent the evening with people we never hope to meet again.

rv.cn: John R. Ziegler and Leah Richards
rv.q: The gripping, sensitive performances by the cast ensure that the audience experiences each woman as a distinct, layered person.
Benevolent is a powerful play, strikingly well directed, with turns and revelations that land forcefully, even if one can see them coming.

cn.t: McIntosh's historical drama about women in a 1917 reformatory earns strong praise for its nuanced blend of dark humor and genuine emotion, with critics highlighting four superb performances and riveting exploration of female confinement.
